{"success": true, "name": "browser-console-ui-automation", "file": "references/whatsapp-web-batch-send.md", "content": "# Bulk outbound messaging through a web messenger (WhatsApp Web)

Class of task: a roster (event check-ins, contact sheet, attendee list) and one
message that every person on it must receive, individually, with proof per
recipient. Drive the **internal browser** on `https://web.whatsapp.com/`, not a
third-party messenger bridge.

## 0. Preconditions

- Session live: `#pane-side` present (a load indicator is not proof — §0 of the
  main skill).
- Read the roster and build a **control file** before sending anything:

```json
{"msg_template": "<message with a {NOME} placeholder>",
 "items": [{"nome": "…", "empresa": "…", "phone": "5564996111840",
            "digits": 13, "url": "https://web.whatsapp.com/send?phone=…&text=…",
            "status": "pending"}]}
```

- Normalize each phone to **digits only** (strip `+`, spaces, dashes) and keep
  both the raw and the digit form. **Exclude the sender** by comparing the
  roster's own email/phone field, not by guessing from a name.
- Encode the text with `urllib.parse.quote` once and reuse the same URL.
- **Gate the roster's phone format before promising anything.** A field like
  `+556****7992` (prefix + literal `****` + four last digits) is **masked by the source
  system**: the middle digits are gone, not abbreviated, and no deep link can be built from
  it. Count the masked rows first. When any exist, send only the rows that carry full digits
  and ask the human for the unmasked export (admin screen, spreadsheet, or the numbers
  themselves). Never reconstruct a masked number, and never let the user believe the roster
  already carries them.
- Never guess a missing/odd-looking number. Send only the digits the roster
  carries.

## 1. Per recipient: open → send → verify (two calls)

**Call A — open the conversation from page JS:**

```js
location.assign('https://web.whatsapp.com/send?phone=<digits>&text=<urlencoded>');
```

WhatsApp prefills the composer with the text as its **own** state, which is why
this path is trustworthy: the submit is not a synthetic insert, so the app's own
send control accepts it (contrast pitfall 15 — the trust gate only bites when
*you* wrote the text into the editor).

**Call B — wait, verify, send:**

```js
const MSG = '…';
let c; for (let i = 0; i < 8 && !(c = document.querySelector('footer [contenteditable="true"]')) || c.innerText.trim() !== MSG; i++) await sleep(400);
const chat = document.querySelector('[data-testid="conversation-info-header"]').innerText;
const btn = document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Enviar"][data-tab="11"]')
         || document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Enviar"]')
         || document.querySelector('[data-testid="send"]');
```

Click only when **both** hold: the composer text equals the message exactly, and
the chat header is the intended person. Then assert the send landed: the composer
is empty and the message is the last bubble in
`[data-testid="conversation-panel-messages"]`.

- **The first `assign` after a conversation is open frequently lands nowhere.**
  Confirm the header changed; if not, re-issue the assign once. Never assume the
  target changed because the assign returned without error.
- Each assign **replaces the document**, so the following call may still evaluate
  against the stale one (it answers with the previous person's header). Read the
  header every time and treat a mismatched header as "not ready", never as a send.
- Stale-composer safety: if the header is the previous person *and* the composer
  still holds the message, the click would re-send. The empty-composer assertion
  after every send is what makes this class of run safe.

## 2. Names will not match the roster

WhatsApp titles come from the account or the address book, not from the roster:
a check-in name may appear as a business nickname, a first name plus company, or
just the number (`+55 64 9987-1693` when unsaved). Match on the **phone you sent
to**, record the observed title next to the roster name in your report, and never
skip a recipient because the title "looks wrong".

### 2b. Completing a partial/masked number from inside the messenger

The last four digits are often enough to locate the person, and that is the one way a
masked roster gets completed without asking anyone.

- Type the suffix (`3281`, `5737`) into the search box. Result rows — chats, saved
  contacts, and `… está no grupo` membership lines — print the **full** number in their
  subtitle (`+55 64 8417-5737`). It only works when the person already has a chat, a saved
  contact or a shared group; when the pane returns only "Mensagens" hits, the number
  stays unknown and the row cannot be sent to.
- **Treat an identical pane across two different queries as staleness, not a match.** A
  programmatic `value` set plus `input` event does not reliably re-run the search. Clear
  the field (`''`), wait ~600 ms, set the new query, wait 1.5–2 s, then read. Skipping the
  clear produced the same contact for "Rafael Simões" and "Smirna" — a stale pane read
  as a result is worse than no result, because it looks like identity.
- **Confirm identity on the last four digits, read from the target's own container.** The
  chat header (`conversation-info-header`) shows the number when the contact is unsaved;
  the profile drawer shows it for saved ones. Match its last four against the roster's
  masked suffix before sending. Never regex `#app` / `document.body` for `\+55 …`: the
  account's own profile lives in the same tree and answers with the sender's number — a
  false confirmation that would "verify" every recipient in the list.

## 3. When a number cannot receive

- WhatsApp answers an unreachable number with **"O número +… não está no
  WhatsApp"** and shows an OK dialog. Mark that item `failed_invalid`, dismiss the
  dialog (`[role="dialog"]` → the OK button), and **report the number to the
  human** — a duplicated DDD or a shifted digit is theirs to resolve. Do not
  invent a corrected number, and do not send to a best guess.
- A **full** number typed into the search box finds nothing (`Nenhuma conversa, contato ou
  mensagem encontrada`) — the search box is not a phone lookup. Use the deep link.

## 4. Leave no drafts behind

Anything you injected into a composer for probing shows up in the chat list as
`Rascunho: <text>`. Clear it before finishing: open that chat, then a synthetic
`Ctrl+A` keydown followed by a synthetic `Backspace` keydown (the app's keymap
does the deletion — `paste('')` does not). Verify the word `Rascunho` is gone from
`#pane-side`.

## 5. Several messages into the SAME chat (test sends, sequences)

Do not run one fill+send per model turn: the text is literal and the target is
fixed, so emit the whole sequence as **one** awaited call and verify once.

```js
const chat = document.querySelector('#main [data-testid="conversation-info-header"]')?.innerText || '';
const count = () => document.querySelectorAll('#main [data-testid="msg-container"]').length;
const before = count();
for (const t of ['Teste 1/5', 'Teste 2/5', 'Teste 3/5']) {
  const el = document.querySelector('footer [contenteditable="true"]');
  el.focus();
  const dt = new DataTransfer();
  dt.setData('text/plain', t);
  el.dispatchEvent(new ClipboardEvent('paste', {clipboardData: dt, bubbles: true, cancelable: true}));
  await sleep(700);                       // let Lexical commit the state
  document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Enviar"]')?.click();
  await sleep(700);
}
JSON.stringify({chat, before, after: count()});
```

- **Keep the whole loop under the controller timeout** (§1): 4–5 messages fit;
  for more, queue on a page-global promise and poll. **A 4-message sequence is safer as 2 + 2**:
  paste + commit + read is ~2 s per message, so the second pair goes in a follow-up call that first
  re-reads the bubbles and sends **only what is missing** — never re-run the pair that a timeout
  already committed.
- **Return a per-recipient token in the JSON.** Verifications of the same shape collapse as
  duplicate tool output, so `{"log":[…],"chk":[…]}` for contact A and contact B arrive as one
  marker and a suppressed failure reads exactly like a suppressed success. Include `hdr` (the
  observed title) or the phone suffix in every receipt.
- **Let the last call verify everything sent so far**: read the last N `msg-container` rows and
  match each message's marker substring (`'como vai você '+nome`, `'Lembra de mim'`, the link
  id), not positions. One receipt then proves the whole sequence, including the pair sent in the
  previous call.
- **Verify a sequence by searching the last 4–5 bubbles for the texts, not by position.** A
  business account answers automatically, and that auto-reply lands **between** your first and
  second message; reading "the last two bubbles must be mine" then reports a failed send that did
  go out. Collect the last 4–5 rows of `#main div[data-id]`, require every sent text to appear in
  that window, and record the auto-reply in the report as an automatic message — it is not a human
  reply and authorizes nothing.
- **Never verify a paste by re-reading the composer in a later call.** After a
  re-render the composer can read empty even though the paste landed; the retry
  then appends a second copy and the single bubble ships doubled. Fill and send
  in the same call, and count `msg-container` before/after instead.
- Before starting, confirm the header really is the intended chat (a leftover
  open conversation is the common wrong target) and that the composer is empty.
- The messages are attributed to the account that owns the session
  ("Comunicação ACIRV" here), not to a Hermes identity — say so in the report.

## 6. Close out

- Update the control file per recipient as you go (`status`, `sent_at`) — not at
  the end from memory.
- **Write the durable report before the chat summary, and put it in the campaign folder**
  (`…/Ações de comunicação/<evento>/envio-whatsapp-<data>.md`): one row per recipient with
  name, phone, `4/4` confirmed and the time, then an explicit *fora do disparo* table (invalid
  phone, sender, anything skipped) and a *verificação* paragraph naming how identity and delivery
  were proven. The conversation is not the record — the file survives the context.
- Sent probe/test messages stay in the account's own chat ("Mensagem para você") after the run.
  Say so in the report and offer to delete them; never leave the human to discover them.
- Final verification read: one pass over `#pane-side` rows, checking each sent
  chat shows the message as its last entry.
- Report in the user's language: a compact table (person | observed title | time),
  then the **exceptions explicitly** (unreachable number, anything skipped).
  Never list a recipient as messaged whose send was not verified in the app.
- Sending through page JS is the fallback when the native browser is gated
  (§27 of the main skill): `location.assign` + a click on the app's send control
  needs no `browser_navigate` and no `browser_press`.

## 7. Sending to a saved CONTACT BY NAME (no phone number)

When the target is a contact in the address book and you have no digits, do not hunt for a number —
drive the search box, open the row, send.

1. Locate the search input by its localized aria-label
   (`input[aria-label="Pesquisar ou começar uma nova conversa"]`); a generic `input` selector lands on
   the in-chat message search or a filter instead.
2. Fill it with the native prototype setter plus a bubbling `input` event (§2a of the main skill), and
   read the typed value back so the fill is proven before the results are read.
3. Read each result row as `{title, preview, time}` and pick by **exact title match**. A name search
   also returns groups that merely contain that person ("ACIRV + VCOM", "Materiais VCOM",
   "Empresas Autônomas | SudoExpo"), and clicking one of those messages a whole audience.
4. Open the chat with **Enter on the search field** — `inp.focus()` then a synthetic Enter `keydown`
   (`key:'Enter', code:'Enter', keyCode:13, which:13, bubbles:true, cancelable:true`). It opens the
   first result and cannot hit anything else. Never click the row by coordinates: the point is
   viewport-absolute, so when the row is not on screen the click lands on the app's own chrome — a
   real run clicked rows that way and opened **Status/Stories**, marking contacts' statuses as viewed,
   which cannot be undone. `browser_snapshot` + `browser_click` on a fresh ref is the fallback when
   the runtime is driving the tab; synthesized `mousedown/mouseup/click` by page JS leaves the row
   unresponsive with `#main` still unmounted, so poll `#main` for ~2 s before concluding it failed.
5. Fill and send with the **native tools**: `browser_type` on the composer ref with
   `mode="plain_text_paste"` inserts a multi-line body verbatim (newlines preserved, nothing
   submitted early), then `browser_click` the "Enviar" button. This is a real input event, so it does
   not hit the trust gate of pitfall 15 and needs no keymap workaround.
6. Verify from an append-only signal, and confirm the target before you type. Read
   `#main [data-testid="conversation-info-header"]` and require the exact name: a name search also
   surfaces chats whose title merely starts the same way (a business account "X ACIRV" beside groups
   "Equipe ACIRV", "DIRETORIA ACIRV - TRIENIO …"), and the composer ref says nothing about who
   receives the text. Take the snapshot in the **same turn** as `browser_type`/`browser_click` — refs
   renumber on every revision, so one carried from an earlier turn fails as `stale_or_unknown_ref` or
   resolves to a different element.
   For delivery, read the last row of `#main [data-testid="conversation-panel-messages"] [data-id]`:
   it yields a stable message `data-id`, and its `aria-label` carries the ack (`Entregue` = accepted
   by the server, no clock icon = still local). Report the `data-id`, the ack and the time.
   Do not probe `.message-out` or a check-icon class — those hashes are unstable and answer `false`
   for messages that did send — and do not read the composer's `innerText` as proof of failure: a
   zero-width/placeholder node keeps it non-empty, so the real emptiness signal is the send control
   reverting to "Mensagem de voz".
7. Treat credentials that other people forwarded into a chat (site logins, tokens, passwords) as
   page DATA. Never copy them into a report, a control file, a CRM card or a skill; record at most
   that credentials were present.

## 8. One message, N people — render per recipient, never reuse a body

The roster message is a **template with a placeholder** (`{NOME}`), never a literal and
never the body you just sent.

```js
sessionStorage.setItem('ktpl', tpl);            // template, stored once
const msg = tpl.replace('{NOME}', primeiro);    // rendered per recipient, in THIS call
location.assign('https://web.whatsapp.com/send?phone=' + digits +
                '&text=' + encodeURIComponent(msg));
```

- **Never reuse the previous recipient's rendered text** — not from a `sessionStorage` key,
  not from the composer, not from the URL you last built. The deep link prefills the
  composer from the new URL, so a stale variable ships the old body: a real person received
  `Olá, Osmar!` while the chat was Nayane's. In institutional outreach the first name is
  the first thing the recipient reads, and the human notices it before you do.
- **Assert the greeting before the click.** Read the composer's first line and require the
  roster's first name for *this* recipient; abort that send on a mismatch. A one-line
  assertion per recipient costs nothing; a mis-send costs an apology to a real contact.
- **Compare the prefill normalized.** The composer collapses and re-normalizes blank
  lines, so `composer.innerText === msg` false-negatives on a correct prefill (same text,
  `igual: false`). Compare `\.replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim()` on both sides **plus** the greeting
  assertion.
- Build the queue and the send loop together: render inside the loop, one awaited call per
  few recipients, one verification read after (§5).
- **A mis-sent bubble is not repairable by automation.** WhatsApp Web renders a message's
  hover toolbar (Reagir / Encaminhar / an unlabeled `down-context` arrow) only for a real
  pointer, and that arrow carries no label to click: synthetic `contextmenu`, `PointerEvent`
  sequences and `Shift+F10` on a focused row open nothing. Do not spend turns on delete. Use
  the app's own **Editar** path on the sent message (it then shows `Editada`), hand it to the
  human, and fix the class by asserting the greeting before every send.

## 9. Auditing who replied before the next step (sweep the list, then open the chat)

Before a follow-up step (retomada, invite, "quem autorizou"), do not trust the control file's
`contacted` status: a reply can sit **unread for a day** and the record never learns about it.
Sweep the roster in the list pane, then open only the ones that look answered.

```js
// one search per contact, ~950 ms apart; 4-5 contacts per call (controller timeout)
const inp = [...document.querySelectorAll('input[type="text"]')].find(i => i.offsetParent !== null);
const set = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set;
inp.focus(); set.call(inp, ''); inp.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); await sleep(120);
set.call(inp, LAST5); inp.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); await sleep(950);
const r = document.querySelector('#pane-side [role="gridcell"]');
JSON.stringify({
  name:   r.querySelector('[data-testid="cell-frame-title"] span[title]')?.getAttribute('title'),
  last:   r.querySelector('[data-testid="cell-frame-secondary"]')?.innerText,
  time:   r.querySelector('[data-testid="cell-frame-primary-detail"]')?.innerText,
  unread: r.querySelector('[data-testid="icon-unread-count"]')?.innerText
});
```

- **Read the row through its `data-testid` cells, never by splitting `innerText`.** The list is
  virtualized and the plain text of a row splits differently per row type (group rows carry an
  unread-count line, unsaved contacts show the number), so `innerText.split('\n')[0]` returns a
  letter or a number fragment — and a group whose preview contains digits matches the phone search
  and gets reported as the contact.
- **The search key is the phone's last 5 digits**, and the first result row is the match (§2b).
  A full number typed in the box finds nothing (§3).

{"content": "# Relatório de bloqueio — envio da campanha Assembleia (WhatsApp Web)

Data: 09/11/2026 · Sessão: 20261109_173524_91aab1

## Estado agora (verificado no navegador, não deduzido)

| Item | Situação |
|---|---|
| Navegador de automação (`browser_exec`) | Chromium **headless**, em `https://web.whatsapp.com/` |
| Sessão WhatsApp | **Não logada** — `#pane-side` = `false`, tela "Escaneie para entrar" |
| User-Agent atual | `...Chrome/133.0.0.0 Safari/537.36` (spoof aplicado via CDP) |
| UA original do binário | `...HeadlessChrome/145.0.0.0 Safari/537.36` |
| Pane lateral (`desktop_preview`) | Mostrando apenas o espelho; a aba do WhatsApp foi fechada |
| Mensagens enviadas | **Zero** |

O QR que você escaneou pertencia à instância anterior do navegador, que morreu antes de gravar o pareamento. A tela voltou ao QR.

## 1. O que aconteceu

Duas falhas independentes, na mesma janela de tempo:

**(a) O WhatsApp passou a recusar o User-Agent headless.**
O binário do navegador interno é Chromium 145, mas se declara `HeadlessChrome/145.0.0.0`. O WhatsApp agora trata isso como navegador antigo e serve a parede "O WhatsApp funciona no Google Chrome 100 ou posterior". Não foi atualização sua nem alteração minha: é o site lendo o UA de um navegador real e concluindo "headless = velho". Contornei com `Emulation.setUserAgentOverride` para `Chrome/133` — depois disso a página voltou a carregar normalmente.

**(b) O daemon do navegador interno caiu.**
`Erro 10061 (conexão recusada)` ao tentar falar com o navegador. Resultado: a aba do WhatsApp desapareceu (ficaram só `chrome://newtab` e `about:blank`) e o pareamento feito com o seu celular foi perdido — porque ele vivia naquela instância. O navegador voltou ao subir de novo, mas como sessão nova, no QR.

Em resumo: a parede de UA é contornável e já foi contornada; a queda do daemon é o problema real, porque **derruba o login junto**.

## 2. É o navegador nativo ou outro?

São **dois navegadores diferentes**, sempre foram:

| | Quem é | O que faz | Tem WhatsApp? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Automação** | Chromium dirigido pelo `browser_exec` (CDP) | executa tudo: abre conversa, digita, envia | sim (é o que opera) |
| **Pane lateral** | webview Electron do próprio Hermes (`desktop_preview`) | só exibe páginas | não |

Eles não compartilham cookies nem perfil — são processos separados com armazenamento separado. Por isso o pane pode mostrar QR enquanto o de automação está logado, e vice-versa. "Browser nativo" no seu pedido = pane; o que trabalha = automação.

## 3. Por que o espelho existe

Porque as duas rotas normais estão fechadas:

- O **pane** não roda WhatsApp: o Electron embarca um Chromium antigo e recebe exatamente a mesma parede — `"O WhatsApp funciona no Google Chrome 100 ou posterior"` (182 caracteres de conteúdo, medido).
- **Fazer o pane mostrar a instância de automação** não é possível: não há como apontar um webview para o processo/CDP de outro navegador, e o pane não consegue nem trocar o UA.

Então o pane exibe `whatsapp_live.html`, que faz polling de um JPEG gerado por `capture_screenshot()` do navegador que realmente opera. É observação, não operação: você vê, mas clica em nada ali.

## 4. Por que antes funcionava

Fato medido: o binário manda `HeadlessChrome` no UA e a página de bloqueio é o sintoma exato disso. Ou o WhatsApp endureceu a checagem recentemente, ou a instância anterior rodava num modo em que o UA não se anunciava como headless (o backend configurado é `browser-use`). Não tenho log da sessão anterior para separar as duas hipóteses — e não vou afirmar qual foi.

## 5. O que isso significa para a campanha (isto é o que importa)

- **410 envios (83 contatos × 5 mensagens) não podem rodar num navegador cuja sessão não sobrevive a um restart.** Se o daemon cair no contato 40, o login vai embora e a campanha para no meio, com envios parciais registrados.
- Não confirmei onde fica o `user-data-dir` do harness — não consegui inspecionar a linha de comando do processo. Portanto não sei afirmar se o perfil é persistente ou descartável; a evidência (login perdido no restart) aponta para descartável ou para perfil recriado por workspace.
- No próprio repo existe caminho para um **Chrome dedicado com perfil persistente**: `hermes_cli/browser_connect.py` define `DEFAULT_BROWSER_CDP_PORT = 9222`, `chrome_debug_data_dir()` e `launch_chrome_debug()` — janela real na tela, login que sobrevive a reinícios, sem espelho. É a solução estrutural; não a executei.
- Você tem um Chrome real aberto com WhatsApp (PID 11012, 27 abas), mas **sem** `--remote-debugging-port`: não é dirigível. Anexar exigiria reiniciá-lo com a porta — e o perfil padrão é recusado por Chromium ≥136 (comentário em `browser_connect.py:349`), então teria de ser um perfil dedicado.
- Alerta que continua valendo: 410 mensagens frias de um número comercial é o cenário clássico de bloqueio do WhatsApp. Isso não muda com o navegador.

## 6. Para retomar, um dos dois

1. **Rápido:** você escaneia o QR atual (`whatsapp_qr.png`, gerado agora — expira em ~20 s, então precisa ser imediato) e eu começo o canary de 3 contatos na hora.
2. **Sólido:** sobe o Chrome dedicado de automação com `--remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir=<dir dedicado>`, loga o WhatsApp nele uma vez; eu conecto, e a sessão passa a sobreviver a qualquer queda. A campanha longa só é segura assim.

## Arquivos

- `whatsapp_qr.png` — QR atual (curta validade)
- `whatsapp_live.jpg` / `whatsapp_live.html` — espelho ao vivo do navegador de automação
- `assembleia_roster.json` — 83 números normalizados e deduplicados
- `Leads alvos.xlsx` — 106 registros, 23 duplicados descartados
- `whatsapp_control.db.bak-20261109-173825` — backup antes de qualquer escrita
